topic.title: ADK Architecture & Runtimes
topic.slideRef: M0L5 Slides 6–8; M0L9 Slides 6–15; M3L1 Slides 10–19
topic.summary: State prefixes (user:, app:, temp:), Sequential/Parallel output_key, LoopAgent escalate=True, AgentTool vs sub_agents, output_schema trade-offs, Cloud Run ($0 idle) vs Agent Runtime vs GKE.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §5 Trigger #17 | M3L1 Slide 10
questions.q: An ADK developer wants to store a user's preferred language in session state so it persists across multiple conversation sessions for that specific user. Which state prefix should they use?
options: user: (e.g., state['user:preferred_language'])
temp: (cleared after the current invocation)
app: (shared globally across all users of the application)
No prefix (persists only within the single current session)
questions.why: Per Trigger #17: ADK has 4 state scopes: unprefixed (current session only), 'user:' (persists across sessions for that specific user), 'app:' (global across all users), and 'temp:' (cleared after the current invocation).

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §5 Trigger #17 | M3L1 Slide 10
questions.q: In ADK state management, what happens to keys written with the 'temp:' prefix (such as state['temp:scratch_data'])?
options: They exist only during the current invocation (turn) and are automatically cleared when the turn finishes
They persist permanently across all users in VertexAiSessionService
They are automatically exported to BigQuery after 60 minutes
They cause the SessionService to reset the user's conversation history
questions.why: The 'temp:' prefix is for temporary scratch data needed only within the current invocation; ADK clears 'temp:' keys once the invocation completes.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.2 & Tab 3 M0L7 Slides 10–12
questions.q: In a SequentialAgent pipeline, Agent 1 summarizes a report and Agent 2 needs to read that summary in its system instruction. What is the standard ADK pattern?
options: Set output_key='summary' on Agent 1, and reference '{summary}' in Agent 2's instruction
Have Agent 1 write to a local file in /tmp and have Agent 2 call a bash tool
Set include_contents='none' on both agents
Pass Agent 1 inside Agent 2's generate_content_config
questions.why: Setting output_key='summary' saves Agent 1's final response to session.state['summary'], and Agent 2 automatically injects it into its prompt via the '{summary}' placeholder.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.2 & Tab 3 M0L7 Slide 11
questions.q: Two sub-agents inside a ParallelAgent run concurrently and save their outputs to session state. How should you prevent them from overwriting each other?
options: Configure a distinct output_key on each sub-agent (e.g., output_key='data_a' and output_key='data_b')
Configure the exact same output_key on both sub-agents so ADK merges them
Disable SessionService when running ParallelAgent
Set max_iterations=1 on the ParallelAgent
questions.why: Sub-agents in a ParallelAgent execute concurrently against the same session.state, so each branch must write to a distinct output_key to avoid race conditions.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.2 & Tab 3 M0L7 Slide 12
questions.q: How does a sub-agent or tool stop an ADK LoopAgent early before it hits max_iterations?
options: Emit an Event with EventActions(escalate=True) (or set tool_context.actions.escalate = True)
Return None from the LLM prompt
Raise a Python RuntimeError inside the tool
Set disallow_transfer_to_parent=True
questions.why: LoopAgent repeats its sub-agents until either max_iterations is reached or a sub-agent/tool emits an event with escalate=True.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §1.2 & Tab 3 M0L7 Slides 15–18
questions.q: What is the difference between wrapping a specialist agent in AgentTool(specialist) versus adding it to sub_agents=[specialist]?
options: With AgentTool, the parent invokes the specialist like a tool and stays in control; with sub_agents, the parent transfers conversation control to the specialist
With sub_agents, the parent stays in control; with AgentTool, the specialist takes over the conversation permanently
AgentTool only works on GKE, whereas sub_agents only works on Cloud Run
There is no difference; both permanently hand off control to the specialist
questions.why: AgentTool wraps an agent as a callable tool so its answer returns to the parent agent (which stays in control). Listing it in sub_agents delegates/transfers control of the turn.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — Tab 2 M3L1 & Tab 3 M0L6
questions.q: What important limitation applies when you configure output_schema (a Pydantic model) on an ADK LlmAgent?
options: Using output_schema disables tool calling and sub-agent delegation for that agent
Using output_schema disables VertexAiSessionService
Using output_schema requires hand-writing a toolspec.json file
output_schema is only supported on third-party models via LiteLLM
questions.why: In ADK, setting output_schema on an LlmAgent enforces structured JSON output, which disables tool calling and sub-agent delegation for that specific agent.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §5 Trigger #17 | M3L1 Slides 14–19
questions.q: A developer uses before_model_callback as a guardrail to block disallowed prompts before calling Gemini. What should the callback return?
options: Return an LlmResponse object to skip the model call (or return None to allow the model call to proceed)
Return None to block the model call, and return True to allow it
Return a numeric HTTP status code like 403
before_model_callback can only log prompts and cannot skip the model call
questions.why: In before_model_callback, returning None allows the LLM request to proceed normally, whereas returning an LlmResponse object short-circuits the LLM call and returns that response directly.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §5 Triggers #4, #5 & #6 | M0L9 Slides 6–15
questions.q: A customer wants zero compute cost ($0) when their ADK agent sits idle overnight and on weekends. Which runtime should they choose?
options: Cloud Run, because it scales to zero when idle (while Agent Runtime is best when they want turnkey managed sessions and Memory Bank)
GKE with always-on dedicated node pools
BigQuery Provisioned Throughput
Vertex AI Model Registry
questions.why: Per Triggers #4–#6: Choose Cloud Run when the requirement is '$0 compute cost while idle' (scales to zero). Choose Agent Runtime for turnkey managed sessions (VertexAiSessionService) and Memory Bank. Choose GKE for custom networking or self-hosted open models.

questions.docRef: Elevate Capstone Prep (Oct 7-8).md — §5 Trigger #7 | M0L5 Slides 6–8
questions.q: A Google Cloud CE is preparing a live customer screen-share demo of an agentic workflow on a 3P codebase. Should they use Jetski or Antigravity 2.0 (agy)?
options: Antigravity 2.0 (agy), because Jetski is strictly internal-only (google3/Buganizer/Critique) and must NEVER be shown or screen-shared with customers
Jetski, because it is Google's external customer-facing IDE
Either tool, because both are approved for external customer screen-sharing
Neither; live demos can only be run inside HackerRank Secure Mode
questions.why: Per Trigger #7 (M0L5 Slides 6–8): Jetski is exclusively for internal productivity (google3, Buganizer, Critique) and must NEVER be shown to customers. Antigravity 2.0 (agy, authenticated via Argolis) is safe for customer-facing demos and 3P codebases.
